candidates.rationale: Roll back the warehouse_size change to LARGE: since the change, p95 execution on the same statement sources 4,000 ms vs 2,500 ms before (more than +25%, 918 queries). The previous value is restored; no saving is claimed.
No sustained saturation requiring an increase and no strong evidence for a lower ceiling.

Held: the auto_stop_minutes change is applied without a canary, so it waits until its own savings can be priced. At least one step cannot be priced because the current epoch has too little billing history; economics are withheld until it accrues.
Migration is judged on a pre-canary cost comparison, but the current epoch has fewer than 7 days of billing history to price it.

assumptions: Current configuration epoch is the decision baseline.
Forward DBU cost uses the deterministic current-epoch run-rate model.
AWS forward cost is modeled from observed current-epoch resource time and the configured regional price registry when available.
DBU cost is priced at the account's list price; negotiated discounts lower real savings in proportion.
AWS cost is priced at on-demand EC2 rates; Spot, Reserved Instances and Savings Plans are not modeled.

recommended_plan.decision_summary: Plan A — Optimize current warehouse type is the deterministic execution path; apply validation gates and regenerate after invalidating changes. Apply the canary rollback (warehouse_size) before any other step: a change applied first starts a new configuration, and the next run no longer sees the change being rolled back.

reevaluation.method: Later of the active gates: the next settled day, 00:00Z of the analysis date + 1 day (readiness: 2 settled billed days in the current epoch) and 00:00Z of epoch start date + 7 days (cost-history floor). Earliest only: billing ingestion lag, days without billing and query-sample gates can delay it.

portfolio_economics.method: At least one step cannot be priced because the current epoch has too little billing history; economics are withheld until it accrues.
